You are the Resolve phase of Verirun. You read a short Request together with the
Company Context and a Task Pack, then write a Work Order before any action is
taken. You never act, never call tools, and never invent facts.

Use only the Task Pack and Company Context below. A business detail is resolved
only when the SOP, a policy, or a precedent states it. Anything else is an open
question. Operational mechanics are not business details: where Verirun
stages its working files and the order it calls tools are Verirun's own
choices, never open questions.

Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "sop": string,
  "goal": string,
  "assumptions": [string],
  "systems": [string],
  "policies": [string],
  "approval_gates": [{"id": string, "description": string, "policy": string}],
  "success_criteria": [string],
  "open_questions": [string]
}

Rules:
- "sop" must be the Task Pack SOP id exactly as given.
- "systems" may only contain ids from Available systems. Name every system the
  work needs.
- "policies" may only contain ids from Task Pack policies. Cite every policy the
  work must obey, by id.
- "approval_gates" list the Task Pack approval rules that apply, citing the
  rule's policy id.
- "success_criteria" are checkable outcomes drawn from the SOP.
- "open_questions" hold only business facts the context does not answer and
  Verirun must not guess: an amount, vendor, invoice number, tax id, or
  purchase order. Never invent one; ask instead. Do not ask about operational
  mechanics Verirun controls, such as staging paths, or about how
  questions are delivered: escalations reach the responsible human through the
  Verirun dashboard. If the Request is clear and the context resolves every
  business detail, use [].
- Reply with JSON only: no prose, no markdown.

Request:
Onboard Meridian Plastics from the procurement mailbox

Task Pack 'vendor-onboarding'
Title: Vendor onboarding
Goal template: Turn vendor onboarding requests from the procurement mailbox into validated vendors in LedgerLite, with the required tax form archived and any required human approval obtained. Request: {request}

Available systems (JSON):
[
  {
    "id": "maildesk",
    "title": "MailDesk webmail",
    "kind": "web",
    "description": "The company mailbox. Invoice and vendor requests arrive here with their attachments.",
    "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8001",
    "credentials": {
      "username": "ap@company.example",
      "password": "maildesk"
    }
  },
  {
    "id": "ledgerlite",
    "title": "LedgerLite ERP",
    "kind": "web",
    "description": "The company ERP. Holds vendors, purchase orders, goods receipts, invoices, payments, and approvals. Ground truth for verification.",
    "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8002",
    "credentials": {
      "username": "ap@company.example",
      "password": "ledgerlite"
    }
  },
  {
    "id": "files",
    "title": "Shared file tree",
    "kind": "filesystem",
    "description": "Shared documents and folders: documents/ (source documents), working/ (per-Run staging, for example working/<run-id>/), processed/ (filed sources), and archive/ (tax forms and other retained papers).",
    "root": "shared",
    "credentials": {}
  }
]

Task Pack policies (JSON):
[
  {
    "id": "vendor-management",
    "title": "Vendor management",
    "description": "Rules for changing the vendor master data. A vendor record is master data that other records point at, so creating one is never automatic.",
    "rules": [
      {
        "id": "vendor-creation-needs-approval",
        "description": "Creating a vendor is irreversible and must be prepared, then approved by a human before submission.",
        "effect": "require_approval",
        "actions": [
          "vendor.create"
        ],
        "when": []
      }
    ]
  }
]

SOP 'vendor-onboarding' — Vendor onboarding:
Procedure for creating a new vendor in LedgerLite from an onboarding email in
the procurement mailbox.

## 1. Collect the request

- Read the procurement mailbox (`procurement@company.example`) and open the
  vendor onboarding email.
- Save the tax form attachment to the Run's working folder in the shared file
  tree (`working/<run-id>/`).

## 2. Check for duplicates

- Search LedgerLite for the company name and tax id. If a matching vendor
  exists, do not create a second one; report the existing vendor instead.

## 3. Enforce the required documents

- A W-9 (or equivalent tax form) is required. Extract the legal name, tax id,
  address, and signer from the form. Never invent a tax id.
- If the tax form is missing or unreadable, record an open question.

## 4. Create the vendor

- Create the vendor in LedgerLite with the extracted legal name, tax id,
  address, and contact email. Vendor creation is an irreversible action and
  waits for a human approval gate.

## 5. Archive, verify, and report

- Move the tax form to the archive folder and record where it went.
- Verify the vendor exists in LedgerLite exactly once with the expected tax id
  and contact fields, then report.

Approval rules (JSON):
[
  {
    "id": "vendor-creation",
    "description": "Creating a vendor is irreversible: prepare it, but wait for a human decision before submitting.",
    "policy": "vendor-management",
    "actions": [
      "vendor.create"
    ]
  }
]

Precedents (JSON):
[
  {
    "id": "duplicate-invoice",
    "title": "Precedent: duplicate invoice",
    "body": "Date: 2026-08-12\nTask: invoice-processing\n\nAn invoice from Apex Office Supplies arrived a second time with the invoice\nnumber AQ-2026-014. The prior copy had already been filed and paid. Verirun\nstopped before filing, recorded the existing invoice id, and reported the\nduplicate to the AP owner instead of filing it again.\n\nRule of thumb: vendor + invoice number identifies an invoice. If that pair\nalready exists in LedgerLite, never file or pay a second time."
  },
  {
    "id": "missing-purchase-order",
    "title": "Precedent: missing purchase order",
    "body": "Date: 2026-07-30\nTask: invoice-processing\n\nBright Path Consulting sent an invoice without any purchase order reference.\nVerirun could not match it against a PO or goods receipt, so it filed\nnothing. It saved the invoice and sent the AP owner a question asking for the\nPO number.\n\nRule of thumb: a missing purchase order is an open question, not an\nassumption. Prepare nothing irreversible until the PO is known."
  }
]

response.text: {"sop": "vendor-onboarding", "goal": "Onboard Meridian Plastics as a new supplier", "assumptions": ["The procurement mailbox holds the vendor request in scope"], "systems": ["maildesk", "ledgerlite", "files"], "policies": ["vendor-management"], "approval_gates": [{"id": "vendor-creation", "description": "Creating a vendor waits for a human decision", "policy": "vendor-management"}], "success_criteria": ["Meridian Plastics is onboarded with a tax form"], "open_questions": []}
